comment: The document lets a country set up its code lists and data-sharing tools first and decide who manages them later, especially in low-resource areas. But another part (Section 3.6.2) says the main reason health systems cannot share data is that everyone changes the standards their own way. So a country could follow the step-by-step advice, go live with no one yet in charge of the standards, and end up with the exact problem the document warns against.

public.suggestedRevision: State the minimum that must exist before a country switches on its code lists or data-sharing, even at the earliest stage: one named office in charge, a written log of every change, and a way to warn other systems before a code is removed. Allow the "set up first, govern later" path only once this minimum is in place.
